reference: util-linux setsid for bounded waited fixture-owned children, plus an independent Python POSIX session identity assertion. Bash type/help are metadata contracts.
coverage: Waited child argv/environment/output/status; forced-fork session identity; relative missing and nonexecutable children.
Bash type/help metadata, separate from operations.
Default asynchronous lifecycle and controlling-terminal behavior remain deferred.
exclusions: Default asynchronous return timing and -c controlling-terminal setup require a disposable VM/private PTY fixture. No signals are sent.

cases.purpose: Check through Bash's type builtin that this name is registered as a builtin without invoking it.
Check that Bash help publishes the documented invocation and semantics for each supported option; only fixed confirmation text is emitted.
cases.script:
h=$(help setsid)
[[ $h == *'setsid [-w] [-f] [-c] program [args...]'* ]]
[[ $h == *'Run a program in a new session.'* ]]
[[ $h == *'-w, --wait'* && $h == *'-f, --fork'* && $h == *'-c, --ctty'* ]]
[[ $h == *'Without -w, setsid returns immediately and the program runs detached.'* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'documented help fields present'

cases.purpose: Verify the default return timing and compare default versus -f/--fork when the caller is and is not a process-group leader, using a gated child to make waiting observable.
cases.reason: The operation creates a new session and its GNU default fork decision depends on process-group state. A future disposable Linux VM must control the parent PGID, gate and reap the private child, and use an independent helper to record PID/PGID/SID while comparing with GNU util-linux setsid.

cases.purpose: Check -c/--ctty with a private pseudo-terminal, including that the child sees the expected controlling terminal and that setup failure does not execute the helper.
cases.reason: TIOCSCTTY requires a suitable session and terminal. A future disposable Linux VM must provide a private PTY and a helper that reports its controlling-terminal state; no host terminal or terminal driver may be used.

cases.purpose: Compare waited child argv/environment/output and nonzero exit status; no process signals or host sessions are touched.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'printf "env=<%s>\n" "$SESSION_VALUE"' 'printf "arg=<%s>\n" "$@"' 'printf "child stderr\n" >&2' > child
chmod 755 child
export SESSION_VALUE='private environment'
setsid -w ./child '' 'two words' '*'
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'exit 7' > child
setsid --wait ./child

cases.purpose: A missing relative executable returns status 127 in a waited private child.
Independently assert the fixture child becomes its own SID and PGID leader, without emitting variable process IDs.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/python3' 'import os' 'assert os.getpid()==os.getsid(0)==os.getpgrp()' 'print("private-session-leader")' > child
chmod 755 child
setsid --fork --wait ./child

cases.purpose: A waited private nonexecutable file returns status 126.
cases.script:
printf bytes > child
chmod 600 child
setsid -w ./child

cases.purpose: Missing program syntax is rejected before child creation; compare the independent util-linux status and visible diagnostics.
An unknown option is rejected before child creation; retain any util-linux usage-status difference.
